topic: For finite latent-variable causal DAGs with specified observed alphabets, known qualitative functional nodes W, observed support literals Pi, and named x,y, construct FID-S(G,W,Pi,x,y): a terminating graph/support algorithm returning inconsistency, a support-valid formula for P_x(y), or two finite compatible models with identical observed law and unequal target. Prove completeness via a bounded functional-support hedge grammar and support-preserving latent lifting theorem, with explicit certificate/search and rational witness bit-size bounds. Preserve latent-root independence and structural zeros; do not substitute generic real elimination, constrained arithmetic-circuit testing, or the fully observed special case for the latent headline. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: A complete fully observed criterion was derived: on every admissible support, identification is equivalent to agreement of deterministic completions sharing observationally reached CPT rows; disagreement yields common-support rational pairs with denominator at most 8nm and target gap at least 3/4, while agreement gives a guarded g-formula. Exact Fraction checks covered 744 realizable supports, 8,928 query/support cases, and 458 constructed NONID pairs; inconsistent clauses, absent treatment support, intervention-exposed rows, cancellation, and the supported bow were tested, with no current-paper collision found. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove the latent lifting theorem that every residual failure yields a bounded local response obstruction extending to two full independent-latent models with the same observed law/support and different target, and conversely yields a support-valid formula; derive its obstruction grammar and global rational certificate bounds. EARLY KILL TEST: Exhaust the binary graph U->A,B; V->A,C; A->B->C with independent U,V over its 4,096 deterministic skeletons and all observed supports of size at most four for P_{A=a}(C=c); any nonextendable proposed certificate, wrong formula, or proved real separating fiber without a rational pair stops or pivots the run. open_problems.open_problem: For finite latent DAGs with fixed observed alphabets, qualitative functional nodes, and support literals, is there a terminating sound-and-complete algorithm that returns inconsistency, a support-valid formula for P_x(y), or a finite separating model pair?

source_refs.claim: Their F-identification reductions are complete only for stated eliminable classes and positivity conditions, leaving the fully general functional/support problem unresolved.
source_refs.author: Yizuo Chen and Adnan Darwiche

source_refs.claim: They characterize formula-specific positivity requirements and discuss, but do not complete, a positivity-aware identification algorithm.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing functional-ID reductions require eliminability or positivity conditions that need not hold on a support face, while positivity-aware ID tracks only conditions needed by a chosen formula. The prior F-ID+ run likewise left an explicit positive-support residual without a verdict. Neither line supplies a three-way exhaustive procedure when structural zeros, named deterministic mechanisms, and independent latent roots must all be preserved.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite algorithm with a decreasing search rank whose exhaustive terminal outputs are a contradictory support certificate, a guarded identifying functional, or two compatible finite independent-latent SCMs with equal observed law and unequal P_x(y).

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation directly connects qualitative mechanism knowledge, positivity, and completeness of causal identification.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Graph-only ID ignores deterministic mechanism knowledge -> functional information can restore identification -> existing reductions depend on eliminability and positivity -> arbitrary support literals require an exhaustive support-aware decision procedure

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt recursive c-component decomposition, failure localization, and the hedge-based construction proving completeness of ordinary ID.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the canonical formula-or-obstruction completeness architecture that the proposed three-way algorithm must refine.

method_exemplars.technique: Split identification across finitely many control contexts, reduce each labeled graph to ordinary ID, and use the paper's approximation argument in the completeness direction.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Known functional rows create context-dependent edge deletions analogous to control-variable context-specific independence.

method_exemplars.technique: Translate fixing-based identified functionals into weight representations, influence functions, and asymptotically linear estimators.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Each regular success leaf should support a concrete estimator and limit law rather than stopping at symbolic identification.

open_problems.open_problem: Can a finite partial-trace grammar characterize exactly the generalized hedges that survive named functional restrictions, structural zeros, and all cross-context contractions?

source_refs.claim: Classical ID completeness rests on ordinary hedges and unrestricted binary parity mechanisms.
source_refs.author: Ilya Shpitser and Judea Pearl

source_refs.claim: They show ordinary do-calculus criteria are incomplete with general context-specific independences and give only a sound general search.
source_refs.author: Santtu Tikka, Antti Hyttinen, and Juha Karvanen

source_refs.claim: Functional mechanisms can invalidate classical nonidentification conclusions, but their paper supplies no general replacement obstruction grammar.
source_refs.author: Yizuo Chen and Adnan Darwiche

Attack the first genuinely coupled case—two residual districts sharing a sink-row quotient class

open_problems.why_unsolved: A classical hedge witness may alter a node whose function is fixed or place mass on a forbidden support cell. The observed-CSI predecessor additionally found that maximal active deletion can erase every ordinary hedge even though an earlier trace retains a target-changing direction. Thus irreversible pruning is invalid: the grammar must retain enough provenance to coordinate reachable support rows and functional-row equivalences across coupled residual districts.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sound-and-complete finite trace grammar with a decreasing rank, an explicit enumeration bound, a guarded-formula reconstruction map, and a theorem converting every terminal forest-supported obstruction into a global separating pair.

writing_exemplar.why: Its narrative turns every algorithmic failure into one canonical obstruction and proves that no other obstruction is needed.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Hidden confounding creates nonidentifiability -> recursive ID isolates the failing district -> every failure contains a hedge -> functional and support annotations require a trace-refined obstruction language

method_exemplars.technique: Extract nested rooted c-forests from failed recursion and construct parity-based observationally equivalent models.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The new grammar must replace both classical failure localization and the associated model-pair construction.

method_exemplars.technique: Use finite context decomposition and recombination, retaining the context labels that justify each graph reduction.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Functional-support hedge atoms likewise need labels recording which response rows are reachable in each context.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive influence functions from primal and dual fixing representations and construct asymptotically linear estimators.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A stable trace returning a support-valid formula naturally admits this estimation-and-inference rung.

open_problems.open_problem: Does every residual local response obstruction lift to two full finite SCMs with independent latent roots, exact prescribed support, identical rational observed laws, unequal P_x(y), and an explicit certificate bit-size bound?

open_problems.why_unsolved: A target-varying null direction in a finite response kernel need not factor into mutually independent latent-source distributions with shared structural mechanisms. Branching latent ancestors can alter every observed atom and its normalizer, while structural zeros forbid the usual small perturbations. Moreover, a nonempty fiber defined over the rationals need not contain a rational point, so finite parameterization and real separation alone do not yield the requested rational certificate.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Either a constructive support-preserving latent-lifting theorem with explicit latent-cardinality, numerator, denominator, and target-gap bounds for every grammar obstruction, or a smallest finite counterexample showing that a separating fiber requires nonrational parameters or violates source factorization.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames finite latent bounds as the bridge from an infinite latent search to a finite-dimensional closed model while retaining independent sources.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Independent-source latent models appear infinite-dimensional -> finite observed alphabets permit latent-cardinality bounds -> compatibility becomes finite-dimensional -> causal nonidentification still needs exact support-preserving rational witnesses

method_exemplars.technique: Encode hedge paths with latent bits and parity mechanisms so two models agree observationally but separate after intervention.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest constructive separating-pair proof, with support and functional preservation as the changed proof step.

method_exemplars.technique: Apply convex-geometric support lemmas source by source to bound latent cardinalities without collapsing source independence.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired lift must finitely realize an obstruction while preserving mutually independent latent roots.

method_exemplars.technique: Enumerate deterministic response types and express observed-law equality and causal targets as polynomials in independent disturbance probabilities.
method_exemplars.why_closest: These coordinates expose exactly where rationalization must preserve zero cells, all observed equalities, and target separation.

open_problems.open_problem: Can compatibility of a finite observed support with a latent DAG and named qualitative functional nodes be decided by a bounded combinatorial certificate that either constructs an independent-latent model or proves the literals inconsistent?

source_refs.claim: Possible-world diagrams give a complete solution to possibilistic latent causal compatibility, but not intervention identification with prescribed functional nodes.
source_refs.author: Thomas C. Fraser

source_refs.claim: Functional dependencies are qualitative identification inputs, but no complete support-literal consistency calculus is supplied for arbitrary latent DAGs.
source_refs.author: Yizuo Chen and Adnan Darwiche

source_refs.claim: mDAG canonicalization preserves observational marginal models and observed-node intervention structure, but not a support-certificate calculus with fixed functional nodes.
source_refs.author: Robin J. Evans

open_problems.why_unsolved: Possibilistic compatibility decides whether zero and nonzero events can coexist in some latent model, but does not simultaneously impose designated deterministic mechanisms on all response worlds or construct the probabilistic objects needed for P_x(y). Latent canonicalization and functional-ID reductions also do not prove that prescribed support survives their transformations. The missing step is a finite cross-world consistency calculus that respects both source independence and fixed functional rows.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient finite support-world criterion with an explicit size bound, where acceptance constructs an independent-latent SCM realizing exactly the specified support and rejection returns a contradictory finite subset of support and functional literals.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates latent compatibility through finite visible certificates and treats possible worlds as a combinatorial alternative to opaque elimination.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Latent causal hypotheses imply constraints beyond conditional independence -> compatibility is difficult under partial information -> possible-world diagrams make support contradictions finite -> prescribed causal functions require a strengthened support-world calculus

method_exemplars.technique: Construct possible-world diagrams, impose cross-world consistency, quotient by graphical symmetries, and use the convergent finite compatibility hierarchy.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested inconsistency branch is exactly a latent support-compatibility decision augmented by functional-node equations.

method_exemplars.technique: Canonicalize hidden-variable DAGs into mDAGs while preserving observed marginal and intervention models.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Canonical latent representations can bound support-world enumeration without making the certificate depend on irrelevant latent topology.

open_problems.open_problem: Is a binary latent-response witness sufficient for every finite functional-support hedge after embedding it into the specified observed alphabets and support face, or does some smallest obstruction require larger response alphabets?

source_refs.excerpt: Prove an alphabet-lifting or binary-witness sufficiency result
The displayed parity construction is finite and binary

open_problems.why_unsolved: Classical hedge completeness uses a binary parity pair, but fixed observed alphabets, structural zeros, functional rows, and simultaneous observed-law equalities can exhaust its perturbation degrees of freedom. The rejected CS-hedge angles never established alphabet lifting. The first changed proof step is therefore the XOR embedding: each parity coordinate must be routed through the prescribed alphabets without activating forbidden cells or cancelling the intervention contrast.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An alphabet-lifting theorem with an explicit latent-state bound for every functional-support hedge, or a minimal graph/support instance with a proof of binary fiber constancy and a larger-alphabet separating pair.

writing_exemplar.why: Its completeness proof makes the binary parity witness the decisive bridge from a graphical hedge to nonidentification.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Every ordinary ID failure contains a hedge -> a binary parity construction separates the target -> support and functional restrictions constrain that construction -> determine whether binary witnesses remain universal

method_exemplars.technique: Track the binary XOR/parity construction through each rooted-forest layer and isolate the degrees of freedom responsible for observational cancellation and target separation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the exact witness whose sufficiency under support and functional constraints is at issue.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt hedgelet and thicket composition to synchronize local witness components across multiple supplied distributions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Simultaneous-law witness assembly is structurally analogous to embedding one hedge across several support and observational constraints.

method_exemplars.technique: Use canonical response-function representations and cardinality reduction to enumerate the smallest candidate failures of binary sufficiency.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested resolution is explicitly a finite response-alphabet theorem or counterexample.

open_problems.open_problem: For a support-valid identifying functional on a structural-zero face, what is the efficient influence function and regularity frontier when only the denominators actually used by the formula are positive?

source_refs.claim: They derive weaker formula-specific positivity conditions for identification but do not develop semiparametric inference on the resulting support faces.
source_refs.author: Inwoo Hwang, Yesong Choe, Yeahoon Kwon, and Sanghack Lee

source_refs.claim: They derive influence-function estimators for hidden-variable DAG functionals, but not on input-specific structural-zero faces with named functional nodes.
source_refs.author: Rohit Bhattacharya, Razieh Nabi, and Ilya Shpitser

source_refs.claim: They expose the interaction between functional dependencies and positivity at the identification stage, leaving the corresponding estimation theory open.
source_refs.author: Yizuo Chen and Adnan Darwiche

open_problems.why_unsolved: Formula-specific positivity may identify P_x(y) while the observed distribution lies on the boundary of the full simplex. Standard pathwise perturbations can leave that support face, and inverse-weight representations can divide by structurally absent cells. Named functional nodes further restrict the admissible tangent space, so the first missing proof step is a face-restricted tangent-set characterization before the identifying functional can be differentiated.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem characterizing pathwise differentiability on every admissible support face, giving an explicit efficient influence function and cross-fitted asymptotic law when regular, and a regime-specific nonregularity counterexample otherwise.

writing_exemplar.why: It begins from the mismatch between strict positivity and the weaker positivity genuinely required by an identifying formula.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Strict positivity often fails -> formulas may need positivity only on selected events -> positivity-aware ID recovers additional targets -> estimation must respect the resulting lower-dimensional support

method_exemplars.technique: Convert hidden-DAG identifying functionals into weight representations, calculate influence functions, and construct doubly robust or efficient estimators.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The causal target is the same; the changed proof step is calculating the tangent space after imposing structural-zero and functional-model restrictions.

method_exemplars.technique: Track conditional events introduced by do-calculus and Q-decomposition to extract the weakest sufficient positivity condition.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Those events determine which zero cells are harmless and which boundary cells govern estimator regularity.

literature_map:
Shpitser and Pearl (2006, AAAI; 2008, JMLR) give graph-only ID and hedge completeness; their witnesses use unrestricted binary parity mechanisms.
Huang and Valtorta (2006, AAAI) independently prove sound and complete identification for ordinary latent causal Bayesian networks.
Evans (2016, Scandinavian Journal of Statistics, arXiv:1408.1809) gives mDAG canonicalization preserving observed marginal and observed-node intervention models.
Richardson, Evans, Robins, and Shpitser develop nested-Markov fixing machinery underlying modern latent-DAG identification and estimation.
Tikka, Hyttinen, and Karvanen (2019, NeurIPS, arXiv:2009.09768) show ordinary do-calculus search is incomplete with general context-specific independence.
Mokhtarian et al. (2022, AISTATS, arXiv:2110.12064) regain completeness only for context-specific independences controlled by observed roots.
Chen and Darwiche (2024, NeurIPS, arXiv:2403.04919) show qualitative functional nodes can restore identification, but their completeness relies on eliminability and positivity conditions.
Hwang et al. (2024, ICML) derive formula-specific positivity requirements and discuss, without completing, a general positivity-aware ID algorithm.
Fraser (2020, Journal of Causal Inference, arXiv:1902.07091) gives a complete possible-world treatment of possibilistic latent compatibility, the closest combinatorial support-certificate framework.
Rosset, Gisin, and Wolfe (2018, QIC, arXiv:1709.00707) prove finite latent-cardinality bounds while preserving multiple independent sources, but not rational witness bounds.
Duarte et al. (2024, JASA, arXiv:2109.13471) reduce finite discrete causal bounding to polynomial programming and provide numerical epsilon-sharpness rather than symbolic rational certificates.
Finkelstein and Shpitser (2020, UAI) obtain causal bounds from logical counterfactual relations; Sachs, Gabriel, and Sjölander (2022, JCGS) prove symbolic tightness only for a restricted class.
Bhattacharya, Nabi, and Shpitser (2022, JMLR, arXiv:2003.12659) derive hidden-DAG influence-function estimators, but not tangent-space theory on structural-zero faces with designated functional nodes.
No located paper jointly supplies latent confounding, named qualitative functions, explicit support literals, inconsistency/formula/rational-witness output, generalized hedge completeness, and arithmetic certificate bounds.
